The service is called Spotify Terms of Use, and these Terms of Service are effective as of 2024. Here's a plain-language summary:

**Scope**: These Terms govern your relationship with Spotify and apply to all products and services listed on Spotify's official terms page.

**User Content**: Any content you submit to Spotify can be used by the company to improve, operate, and train its AI and machine learning (ML) systems, as long as it's done in accordance with your account settings and applicable laws.

**Privacy**: Spotify's Privacy Policy outlines what personal data is collected and how it's processed. This Terms of Service document doesn't go into specific details, so you'll need to refer to the dedicated Privacy Policy for more information.

**Content License**: Spotify will own the rights to content you submit, unless you explicitly choose to retain ownership through your account settings (though this provision is not defined in detail).

**Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions, which are outlined in the live document.

**Dispute Resolution**: Spotify requires binding arbitration with a class-action waiver for disputes, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

Some clauses to keep in mind:

* Spotify may use your content to train AI and ML systems, which could involve processing and potentially selling anonymized data about your listening habits.
* The Terms require binding arbitration, which means you won't be able to take Spotify to court for disputes. This could limit your ability to seek compensation for damage you sustain.
* The Terms include a class-action waiver, which means that if you're part of a group suing Spotify, your individual claim might be dismissed in favor of an overall settlement.
* The Terms are subject to change, but you might not be directly notified about these changes.

Remember to check Spotify's current terms and conditions page or the Privacy Policy for the most up-to-date information.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SPOTIFY TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Spotify and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added language for AI-generated playlists/'AI DJ', expanded the User Content license to cover user-uploaded audio/podcasts processed by AI features, and updated arbitration and class-action waiver clauses.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Spotify to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.spotify.com/us/legal/end-user-agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.spotify.com/us/legal/end-user-agreement/ .

**Netflix Terms of Use: A Summary**

The Netflix Terms of Use (TOS) govern your relationship with Netflix. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Service Name:** Netflix

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to Netflix's products and services listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** Netflix uses your user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. 
* **Privacy:** While the TOS cross-references Netflix's Privacy Policy, it does not explicitly define how your personal data is used or processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** You agree to binding arbitration with a class-action waiver, except for new accounts which have a 30-day opt-out window. This means you may be giving up your right to a jury trial or class action lawsuit.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement subject to conditions described in the document.
* **Contact:** For questions about these terms, see Netflix's published legal contact information.

**Challenging Provisions:**

* **Binding Arbitration and Class-Action Waivers:** This provision may be limiting, as you may be giving up important rights in case of disputes. Arbitration is a private process instead of a court, and class-action waivers prevent you from joining a lawsuit with other affected users.
* **Use of User-Submitted Content:** While the TOS mentions subject to your settings and applicable law, it doesn't provide clear guidance on how Netflix uses your content, which could be a concern for users who submit sensitive information.

**Important Note:**

The Terms of Service do not explicitly state the types of content allowed on their service or what constitutes a 'Netflix Household', which might cause confusion for users with complex household arrangements.

Overall, the Terms of Service present a standard set of provisions common in online services, but the binding arbitration and class-action waivers may be worrisome for some users.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NETFLIX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Netflix and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected the household sharing/'extra member' policy: paid sharing requires the primary household plus paid additional members, added clearer language on what constitutes a 'Netflix Household', and updated billing/cancellation provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Netflix to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse .

**Service Name:** Disney+ Subscriber Agreement

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms and conditions govern your relationship with Disney+, covering the services and products described on Disney+'s official terms page.
* **Content and License:** Disney+ may use your submitted content to improve its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** Disney+ cross-references its published Privacy Policy, which details the types of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Any disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means you'll give up your right to a trial by court and may be required to settle disputes privately.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Forced arbitration**: The dispute resolution process may be harmful if you feel you've been wronged by Disney+. Arbitration can be biased and may not provide the same protections as a court trial.
* **Class-action waiver**: You may give up your right to participate in class-action lawsuits, which can be more effective in bringing attention to widespread issues.
* **Advertising on ad-free plans**: As of January 27, 2025, Disney+ may begin showing ads on its "no ads" or "ad-free" tiers, which could affect the value of these plans.

**Note:** The Terms of Service do not explicitly address topics such as:

* The potential use of AI-generated content
* Data security in case of a breach
* The specific types of data collected and stored by Disney+

If you're concerned about these or other aspects, it's recommended to review Disney+'s Privacy Policy and contact their legal team for clarification.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DISNEY+ SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Disney+ and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 27, 2025 for new subscribers and March 24, 2025 for existing ones: streaming titles may now show ads even on 'no ads'/'ad free' tiers, expanded arbitration with mass-arbitration procedures following Disney's earlier 2024 Wrongful-Death-case controversy, and updated content-availability language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Disney+ to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement .

**Service Name:** PayPal User Agreement

**Summary:**

These Terms of Service outline the relationship between you and PayPal, the provider of online payment services. The main points of the agreement are:

* **Scope:** These terms apply to PayPal services and products described on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** PayPal uses user-submitted content, if necessary, to function and improve their services. This content can be used in AI/ML systems.
* **Privacy:** The Privacy Policy, linked within these terms, explains what personal data PayPal collects and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** In case of disputes, they primarily require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can end the agreement under specific conditions.
* **Contact:** For questions, see PayPal's published legal contact information.

Some key provisions to consider:
- **Arbitration**: While optional, binding arbitration (a private dispute process) with class-action waivers may limit your ability to join a class-action lawsuit. A 30-day opt-out window for new accounts allows you to opt out of this condition.
- **Data usage**: PayPal may use submitted content to improve their services and AI/ML systems. This data might include personal or financial information.
- **Termination**: Termination can occur if either party breaches conditions or due to unforeseen events, such as regulatory changes.

Keep in mind that binding arbitration can limit your ability to seek redress through the courts and that data usage can raise concerns about data protection. However, these points are standard in many online services agreements. If you have explicit concerns or need further information about these points, consider reviewing PayPal's Privacy Policy and their user agreement closely.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PAYPAL USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Multiple 2024 updates: revised seller-protection criteria, added new fee schedules for cross-border transactions, expanded the dispute resolution / chargeback flow, and clarified handling of cryptocurrency holdings. PayPal publishes upcoming and historical policy diffs at paypal.com/us/legalhub/policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by PayPal to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/useragreement-full . The previous version is available at https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/upcoming-policies-full .

response:
**eBay User Agreement**

These Terms of Service (TOS) govern your relationship with eBay and cover the products and services described on the company's official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License:** eBay uses your user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train its artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The TOS refer to eBay's published Privacy Policy, which outlines the types of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** The TOS require **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with **class-action waivers (meaning you can't join a group lawsuit)**. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts if you don't want to participate in this process.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions outlined in the TOS.
* **Contact:** For questions about these TOS, you can visit the company's published legal contact information.

**Potential Risks to Users:**

* The TOS don't explicitly address user rights if eBay's AI/ML systems misuse or misrepresent your content.
* The **binding arbitration** process may limit your ability to seek redress in a public court or join a group lawsuit.
* The 30-day opt-out window may not give enough time for users to understand their options or make an informed decision about arbitration.

**Review the TOS and eBay's Privacy Policy carefully to understand the details of your agreement and potential risks.**
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — EBAY USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with eBay and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised payments-on-eBay structure for managed payments, added more detailed AI/automated-decision sections, expanded permitted-use language for listing data, and updated arbitration / opt-out procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by eBay to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.ebay.com/help/policies/member-behaviour-policies/user-agreement?id=4259 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.ebay.com/help/policies/member-behaviour-policies/user-agreement?id=4259 .

The Terms of Service outline the rules for using Amazon's products and services. Here's a summary:

**Key Provisions:**

* The terms govern your relationship with Amazon.
* They cover products and services listed on Amazon's official terms page.
* You agree that Amazon can use your submitted content to improve and train their AI/ML systems, as allowed by your settings and applicable law.
* Amazon collects and processes personal data, but this is governed by a separate Privacy Policy.
* Disputes will typically be resolved through binding arbitration with class-action waivers. This means that you likely won't be able to join a class-action lawsuit against Amazon.
* Either party can terminate the agreement, but the specific conditions for this will depend on the live document.
* If you have questions, you can contact Amazon through the provided legal contact information.

**Potential Concerns for Users:**

* **Dispute Resolution:** Binding arbitration with class-action waivers may limit your ability to seek redress through the courts. This could make it more difficult to join class-action lawsuits or seek individual damages.
* **Content Use:** Amazon reserves the right to use your submitted content to train their AI/ML systems. This may be a concern if you're not aware of how your content is being used.
* **Termination:** The specific conditions for terminating the agreement may be outlined in the live document, but this could give Amazon wide latitude to end the agreement for any reason.
* **AI-generated Content:** Amazon uses AI features like Alexa and Rufus, and the terms suggest that generated content may be subject to the user agreement. This may be unclear, and users should review the terms to understand how AI-generated content affects their relationship with Amazon.

Keep in mind that these are potential concerns, and the actual implications of these clauses will depend on the specific language and context.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — AMAZON CONDITIONS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Amazon and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.

response:
**Service Name: Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions**

These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Apple when using their media services, such as iCloud, Apple Music, and the App Store.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all Apple media services you use.
* **Content and License:** Apple can use your submitted content to improve and train their AI systems, but only with your settings and applicable law in mind.
* **Privacy:** Apple's Privacy Policy sets out how they collect and process your personal data.
* **Dispute Resolution:** In case of a dispute, you'll need to go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Apple or you can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions described in the document.

**Noteworthy Clauses:**

* **Binding Arbitration:** Requiring arbitration means you might waive your right to sue Apple in court. While this can be a faster and cheaper process, it might limit your options if you feel Apple has wronged you. 
* **Class-Action Waivers:** You might also be waiving your right to join a class-action lawsuit with others who have similar claims against Apple.
* **Termination:** Apple can terminate the agreement at any time, which might leave you without access to their services.

Overall, these Terms of Service outline how Apple uses your content and personal data, and how they resolve disputes. While they don't explicitly state any clauses that are harmful to users, the arbitration and class-action waiver requirements are worth considering carefully.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — APPLE MEDIA SERVICES TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added explicit references to Apple Intelligence and on-device generative-AI features, clarified content-license scope across services (iCloud, Apple Music, App Store), and revised Family Sharing and Subscriptions sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html .

The service name is iCloud Terms and Conditions. Here's a plain-language summary:

**Service Overview**
iCloud is a cloud storage service provided by Apple. These Terms of Service (TOS) explain how Apple will use your data, what you're allowed to do with the service, and under what circumstances the service can be terminated.

**Key Provisions**

* **Content Submission**: When you use iCloud, Apple may collect content you submit (e.g., photos, emails, documents). Apple can use this content to improve its services, operate its business, or train its AI/ML systems. This is subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Data Protection**: The Privacy Policy governs Apple's collection and processing of personal data. You can find the Privacy Policy document separately.
* **Terms and Dispute Resolution**: Apple may terminate your account at any time, and you can also terminate the agreement with 30 days' notice (subject to certain conditions). To resolve disputes, you're required to participate in binding arbitration, which is a private dispute process instead of going to court. However, if you create a new account, you have a 30-day opt-out window. (This might be considered a bit restrictive, potentially limiting users' options to resolve disputes.)
* **Legal and Safety Exceptions**: Apple may access your stored content under certain circumstances, such as when necessary for safety or legal reasons.
* **Termination**: Either you or Apple can end the agreement by giving notice.

**Harmful Clauses**

* **Binding Arbitration**: This might limit your options to resolve disputes, as it requires you to participate in a private process instead of going to court. However, new account holders have a 30-day opt-out window.
* **Class-Action Waiver**: Apple does not permit you to join a group action lawsuit against the company, which might limit your options to recover damages.
* **Retention of Rights**: Apple can access your content in specific circumstances and retains rights to use such content without asking for your permission.

**Notable Notes**

* The document was last updated in 2024.
* These terms are subject to change (as seen in the Summary of Updated Terms of Service).
* Apple provides contact information at the bottom of the document for questions and concerns about these terms.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ICLOUD TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Advanced Data Protection (end-to-end encryption) language, references to Apple Intelligence Private Cloud Compute, and revised provisions about how stored content may be accessed by Apple for legal/safety reasons.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html .

**Snap Terms of Service Summary**

The terms we're looking at are for the Snapchat service ("Snap"). These Terms of Service (TOS) outline the user's relationship with Snap and cover the products and services described on their official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License**: When you share content on Snap, you grant them permission to use, improve, and train their artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) systems. However, they'll only do this based on your account settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy**: Your personal data is covered by Snap's separate Privacy Policy, which outlines what type of information they collect and how they process it.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most users are required to participate in binding arbitration, which means they'll need to settle disputes through private mediation instead of going to court. However, new accounts have 30 days to opt out. If you create a new account, keep an eye on this period to decide how to proceed.
* **Termination**: Either party can cancel the agreement, but the document says it's subject to specific conditions, which are available in the live document.

**Harmful Clauses to Consider:**

* **Class-action waivers**: As mentioned earlier, Snap has a class-action waiver in place, which can limit your ability to join a group lawsuit if other users face similar issues.
* **Forced arbitration**: Most users are required to engage in binding arbitration, which might not provide as much protection as a court case. Keep in mind the 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

**What's Next?**

If you have any questions about these Terms of Service, you can visit the company's official website at https://www.snap.com/terms for more information. Make sure to review the document carefully before using the Snap services to understand your agreement with them.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SNAP TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Snap (Snapchat) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective April 7, 2025: added new sections on My AI and other generative-AI features, expanded the user-content license for Live/Local/crowd-sourced services, clarified data-sharing with parents (for under-18 users via Family Center), and updated arbitration pre-dispute notice procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Snap (Snapchat) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.snap.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.snap.com/terms .

These are the Pinterest Terms of Service, effective as of 2024.

**Key Provisions:**

- **Scope:** These terms apply to your relationship with Pinterest and any products or services the company offers, as listed on its official terms page.
- **Content and License:** When you create content on Pinterest (like posting a Pin), you give the company permission to use it to improve and train its artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) systems. This is subject to your preference settings and any applicable laws.
- **Dispute Resolution:** If a dispute arises, Pinterest and users must resolve it through binding arbitration with class-action waivers. This means going to private disputes instead of court, and you cannot join a group lawsuit.
- **Termination:** Either party can end this agreement at any time by following the conditions stated in the live document.
- **Privacy:** The terms point you to Pinterest's separately published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed.
- **Contact:** You can find contact information for the company at the same link as these Terms of Service.

**Flagged Clauses:**

- **Dispute Resolution:** While mandatory arbitration can be more efficient, it means users give up the right to a court trial. Also, class-action waivers might limit the ability to resolve disputes collectively.

**Disclaimer:** I'm not providing legal advice.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PINTEREST TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Pinterest and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added language permitting Pinterest to use public Pin content to train AI/ML models for recommendations and safety, clarified obligations for advertisers and merchants, and updated arbitration provisions. Pinterest publishes a public archive at policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Pinterest to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive .

The service name in these Terms of Service is indeed **Tumblr**. Here's a walk-through of the key provisions:

1. **Scope**: These Terms apply to your relationship with Tumblr and the products and services described on their official terms page. This means the rules outlined below govern when you use Tumblr's services.
2. **Content and License**: Tumblr uses your submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, but only as described in the Settings > Visibility > Prevent third-party sharing settings and applicable law.
3. **Privacy**: Tumblr's Privacy Policy (which is separate from these Terms) outlines how it collects and processes your personal data, setting out what categories of data it collects and how it processes it. (However, it's worth noting that the Terms themselves don't provide much detail on this point.)
4. **Dispute Resolution**: If there's a conflict, most updated terms in this set require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. There's a 30-day opt-out window if you're creating a new account, but this only applies to arbitration - not class-action waivers.
5. **Termination**: Either Tumblr or you can terminate the agreement subject to conditions described in the live document.

Some potentially sensitive clauses that may be harmfulto the user include:

* **Dispute Resolution**: binding arbitration and class-action waivers might make it difficult for users to seek justice in a group, or in certain circumstances. The 30-day opt-out window for new accounts is a partial mitigant.
* **Automatic use of public content for artificial intelligence training**: Tumblr can use your public content for AI training without your explicit consent, although you can opt out of this in the Settings.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TUMBLR TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Tumblr and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected Automattic's deal to share public Tumblr posts with AI partners (e.g. for training): added language confirming use of public content for AI training and added a user-facing opt-out (Settings > Visibility > Prevent third-party sharing).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Tumblr to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service .

**Service Name:** Dropbox Terms of Service

**Summary:** These Terms of Service outline the agreement between you and Dropbox (the service provider) for using Dropbox's products and services. The key provisions are:

* **Scope**: These terms apply to any Dropbox product or service mentioned on their official terms page.
* **Content and License**: Dropbox can use your submitted content (like uploaded files) to operate, improve, and train its AI systems, based on your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy**: Your personal data is processed in accordance with Dropbox's published Privacy Policy. They collect certain categories of personal data, which are described in that policy.
* **Dispute Resolution**: If a dispute arises, binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) may be required, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

**Harmful Clauses to Note:**

* **Dispute Resolution**: The requirement for binding arbitration with class-action waivers may limit your ability to bring or participate in a class-action lawsuit against Dropbox. This could potentially disadvantage users who might benefit from a group action.
* **Dispute Resolution's 30-day Opt-Out**: New account holders only have a 30-day window to opt-out of mandatory arbitration. If you don't take action within 30 days, you'll be bound by this requirement.

Keep in mind that these Terms of Service don't address everything, but they provide a solid foundation for understanding your relationship with Dropbox.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DROPBOX TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Dropbox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Late-2023/early-2024 update added Dropbox AI features (Dropbox Dash, AI search/summary). After user backlash, Dropbox amended language (Dec 2023 / 2024) to explicitly state customer data is not used to train third-party AI models without consent.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Dropbox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.dropbox.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230601000000*/https://www.dropbox.com/terms .

**Summary of Canva Terms of Use:**

The Canva Terms of Use govern your relationship with Canva and apply to the products and services offered on the Canva website. The updated terms, effective 2024, outline agreements between Canva and its users.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all Canva products and services listed on the company's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Canva, you agree to how it's used by the company to operate and improve its services.
* **Ownership:** If you use Canva's generative AI tools (such as Magic Studio), you own any output you create, but Canva may still hold some rights to it.
* **Privacy:** Canva's published Privacy Policy explains how your personal data is collected and processed.
* **Termination:** Either party can cancel the agreement under specified conditions.

Potential Concerns:

* **Content Moderation:** As part of using Canva's AI tools, there are new requirements for content-moderation and labeling.
* **Arbitration:** The terms require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, although there's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. Arbitration means using a private dispute resolution process instead of going to court.
* **Restrictions on AI Use:** You are not allowed to use Canva-generated content to train other AI models.

Note: These potential concerns may seem complex, but we can discuss them further if you have any questions.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — CANVA TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Canva and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Canva's generative AI tools (Magic Studio): users own outputs subject to platform rights, restrictions on using Canva-generated content to train other AI models, and new content-moderation/labeling requirements.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Canva to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ .

[USER_FAVORABLE]

- Section 3 — restrictions on using Canva-generated content to train other AI models protect creators
[EXPECTED SUMMARY POINTS]
- The updated terms take effect in 2024 and replace the 2023 version.
- Key change: 2024 update added rules for Canva's generative AI tools (Magic Studio): users own outputs subject to platform rights, restrictions on using Canva-generated content to train other AI models, and new content-moderation/labeling requirements.
- The new terms govern Canva Terms of Use for users of Canva.
- Users should review the cross-referenced Privacy Policy to understand data handling.
- The previous version of the terms is available for comparison at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/.

These are the Terms of Service for Notion, a productivity and note-taking service. 

**Key Provisions:**

* The Terms of Service describe the rules and guidelines for using Notion services, which includes using Notion's products and services.
* When using Notion, you grant them the right to use your submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* The service emphasizes that they collect personal data from their users, which is governed by Notion's Privacy Policy. 
* Any disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), and users may opt-out within 30 days for new accounts (exceptions apply).
* Either party can terminate the agreement according to conditions stated in the document.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Binding Arbitration**: This means that in the event of a dispute, you'll have to resolve it privately through arbitration, rather than going to court. Some users may consider this restrictive or potentially unfair to their interests.

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NOTION TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Notion and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Notion AI provisions (input/output ownership, no training of foundational models on customer data by default), updated subprocessor list, and clarified data-residency options for enterprise plans.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Notion to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.notion.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.notion.so/terms .

**Service Name:** Figma

**Key Provisions:**

These Terms of Service outline the relationship between Figma and users. Here are the key points:

* **Scope**: These terms govern how Figma uses its products and services.
* **Content and License**: Figma uses user-submitted content to improve and train its AI and machine learning (ML) systems, but only with your settings and applicable law.
* **Content is used to train AI/ML systems**: User content may be used to train AI and ML systems, including third-party models. However, Figma states that they will only do so with opt-in.
* **Privacy**: The company refers to its published Privacy Policy to explain how personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most terms require binding arbitration with class-action waivers. This means that any disputes would go to a private process instead of court (see [binding arbitration](#)).
* **Termination**: Either Figma or the user can terminate the agreement if the live document's conditions are met.

**Clauses to be aware of:**

*  **Figma may use third-party AI models**: Figma states that they will only use third-party generative models with opt-in. However, users should be aware that this may change in the future.
* **No guarantees about AI/ML training**: Although Figma says they'll use opt-in for third-party models, they don't explicitly state what happens to content beyond their own systems.
* **No court representation**: Binding arbitration (a private dispute process)(#) can be detrimental to users, especially if they have limited financial resources or power against large corporations.

**Notes:**
If you have any concerns about your rights or the potential impact of these Terms of Service, it might be best to consult a legal professional. These notes are based on the provided version of the terms.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FIGMA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Figma and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Figma AI features (Make Designs, Visual Search) provisions, clarified that customer file content is not used to train third-party generative models without opt-in, and updated security and incident-notification language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Figma to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.figma.com/legal/tos/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.figma.com/tos/ .

service_name: Stack Overflow Public Network Terms of Service
response:
The service is called the Stack Overflow Public Network Terms of Service, and these terms outline the agreement between you and Stack Overflow when using their products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* These terms apply to the products and services described on Stack Overflow's official terms page.
* When you post content, like questions and answers, on Stack Overflow, it can be used by the company to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, depending on your settings and applicable law.
* Your personal data is collected and processed as described in Stack Overflow's published Privacy Policy.

**Important Clauses:**

* You grant Stack Overflow a license to use your posted content, specifically under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike (CC BY-SA) license.
* However, there are restrictions on using or extracting the content for training generative AI or LLMs without a commercial agreement with the company. This means you might not be allowed to use Stack Overflow content for certain AI training purposes unless you have a specific agreement with them.
* If you have a dispute with Stack Overflow, you and the company agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of going to court) with class-action waivers, unless you opt out within 30 days of creating your account.
* Either Stack Overflow or you can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions described in the live document.

**Potential Harm:**

* The restriction on using Stack Overflow content for AI training without a commercial agreement might limit your ability to use their content for certain AI applications.
* The binding arbitration clause with class-action waivers may not allow you to join a class-action lawsuit against Stack Overflow, potentially limiting your ability to seek redress for certain grievances.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STACK OVERFLOW PUBLIC NETWORK TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Stack Overflow and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: May 2024 update added a 'Generative AI / LLM' restriction explicitly licensing posted Q&A under CC BY-SA but limiting bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement, after the company's content-licensing deals with OpenAI and Google.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Stack Overflow to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public .

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to Quora's products and services.

* **Binding Arbitration with Class-Action Waivers:** This clause may limit your ability to participate in group lawsuits against Quora, which could be a concern if you think your rights are being violated.

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — QUORA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Quora and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Poe (Quora's AI chatbot platform): user prompts/responses may be used to improve Poe and partner models subject to settings, added bot-developer terms, and revised dispute resolution.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Quora to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.quora.com/about/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.quora.com/about/tos .

**Service Name:** 23andMe Terms of Service

**Key Provisions:**

The 23andMe Terms of Service govern the relationship between 23andMe and its users. Here's a breakdown of key points:

* **Scope:** These terms apply to the products and services described on 23andMe's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** 23andMe uses user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI and ML systems, in accordance with user settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The terms reference 23andMe's published **Privacy Policy**, which outlines the types of personal data collected and how it is processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes need to go through **binding arbitration**, where users waive the right to class-action lawsuits and have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. 
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement based on conditions outlined in the live document.

**Clauses That May Be Harmful to Users:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration Clause:** If you don't opt out, you'll have to go through binding arbitration for certain disputes, which may limit your rights to sue for breach-related claims. This includes a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Class Action Waivers:** By agreeing to these terms, you give up your right to join or participate in class-action lawsuits against 23andMe.

These changes may affect users who don't write to opt out or take action within the stated timeframe.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

response:
**Service Overview**

The Terms of Service outline the user agreement with Twitch, a live streaming and video sharing platform. The Terms define the rules for interacting with Twitch and its services, including content submission, data collection, and dispute resolution.

**Key Provisions**

Here are the key points from the Terms of Service:

* **Scope**: These Terms apply to the user's relationship with Twitch and its products and services, as described on the official terms page.
* **Content and License**: Twitch uses user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems. The user retains ownership of their content, but Twitch can use it to generate revenue and improve the service.
* **Privacy**: The Terms cross-reference Twitch's published Privacy Policy, which explains how the company collects and processes personal data.
* **Dispute Resolution**: To settle disputes, users must participate in binding arbitration, which is a private dispute process outside of court. This means users cannot file a lawsuit against Twitch, and the decision will be made by an arbitrator rather than a judge or jury. **Note: This may limit the user's ability to seek justice in court.**
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement if conditions are met, as described in the live document.

**Harmful Clauses**

response:
The Terms of Service governs the relationship between you and Roblox, and apply to its products and services.

Key provisions:

* **Default settings for minors**: If you're under 13, your account is private by default. You need parental consent to change this setting.
* **Content and usage**: You understand that any content you submit can be used by Roblox to improve and train their AI/ML systems, but only according to your settings and applicable law.
* **Dispute resolution**: Most terms require **binding arbitration** with **class-action waivers**, meaning disputes are settled outside of court and individual cases can't join together in a class action lawsuit. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under the conditions described in the document.
* **Privacy**: The Terms of Service reference Roblox's Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed.

**Potential concerns for users:**

* **Lack of transparency**: The Terms of Service doesn't clearly explain how user data is used, except to reference the Privacy Policy.
* **Dispute resolution**: Requiring binding arbitration with class-action waivers might limit your options in case of a dispute.
* **Termination**: The Terms of Service allow either party to terminate the agreement without providing clear reasons or procedures.

Note: The Terms of Service don't address certain topics, such as what happens to your account if you delete a game or how copyright claims are handled.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ROBLOX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Roblox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update strengthened minor-protection language (default-private accounts under 13, parental-consent flows), updated Robux/DevEx provisions, added rules for Roblox's generative-AI 'Studio Assistant' and avatar-creation tools, and revised arbitration class-waiver section.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Roblox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 .

response:
The Terms of Service govern the use of the Steam Subscriber Agreement. 

**Key Provisions:**

- **Scope:** These terms apply to Steam and its services. You agree to these terms when you use Steam.
- **Content and License:** When you upload content to Steam, you grant the company permission to use that content for various purposes like improving Steam's AI and ML systems (subject to your settings and applicable law).
- **Privacy:** Steam's Privacy Policy describes what personal data is collected and how it's used. While this policy isn't directly part of the terms, you may want to review it as well.
- **Dispute Resolution:** If a dispute arises, Steam may insist on binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) involving class-action waivers, unless it's in the US or another country with specific exceptions. 
However, in a notable change, Steam has removed mandatory arbitration for disputes in the US.
- **Termination:** Either Steam or you can terminate the agreement following the conditions listed in the terms.
- **Contact Information:** If you have questions, see the company's published legal contact details - currently, this is available at the link listed in the terms.

**Potential Concerns:**

* In countries or states with no clear exceptions to binding arbitration and class-action waivers, you might not have access to traditional court proceedings.
* By uploading content, you grant Steam significant permission that might be difficult to revoke if they decide to use your content.
* The removal of mandatory arbitration in the US is a positive change, but binding arbitration is still the default in most cases.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STEAM SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Steam (Valve) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: September 26, 2024 update removed the mandatory arbitration / class-action waiver clauses entirely - Valve now requires disputes to be filed in court (subject to venue rules), reversing several years of arbitration-only language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Steam (Valve) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/ .

Epic Games Terms of Service govern your relationship with Epic Games, the company behind popular games like Fortnite. These terms outline the rules and expectations for using Epic Games' products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope**: These terms apply to the products and services listed on Epic Games' official terms page.
2. **Content and License**: You grant Epic Games a license to use content you submit, subject to your settings and applicable law. This includes using it to improve and train the company's AI/ML systems.
3. **Privacy**: Your personal data is governed by Epic Games' Privacy Policy, which you can find by linking to the company's website.
4. **Dispute Resolution**: Most agreements require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. 
5. **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under the conditions described in the live document.
6. **Contact**: If you have questions about these terms, see Epic Games' published legal contact information.

**Potential Concerns:**

1. **Data Use and AI Training**: Epic Games can use your submitted content, including account information, to train AI/ML systems, which could raise concerns about data ownership and control.
2. **Binding Arbitration**: This clause requires you to resolve disputes through private arbitration, which may limit your access to a court of law.
3. **Class-Action Waivers**: This provision means you won't be able to join a class-action lawsuit if there are similar issues with multiple users.

These concerns point to the importance of understanding what you're agreeing to and being aware of your data rights.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — EPIC GAMES TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Epic Games and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised the Fortnite/Epic Account language, added User-Generated Content (UEFN) provisions and creator-payout rules, updated EU-specific consumer-rights language post-DMA, and refreshed dispute-resolution sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Epic Games to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos .

**Service Name:** DoorDash Consumer Terms of Service

**Summary:** These Terms of Service govern your relationship with DoorDash, a food delivery and ordering platform. They cover its products and services, govern how user-submitted content is used, and outline the dispute resolution process. The Terms require binding arbitration for disputes (a private dispute process instead of going to court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope and Relationship:** These Terms apply to your use of DoorDash's products and services, including food delivery and ordering.
* **User-Submitted Content:** DoorDash uses your content, such as reviews and ratings, to operate and improve its services. Your settings and applicable law dictate how this data is used.
* **Privacy:** DoorDash references its Privacy Policy for information on the categories of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** You must go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) for disputes, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means you give up your right to go to court for disputes.
* **Termination:** Either DoorDash or you can terminate the agreement, but the conditions for this are found in the live document.
* **Contact:** For questions about these Terms, visit DoorDash's website at the terms URL.

**Clauses that may be harmful to users:**

* **Binding Arbitration:** This requirement for private dispute resolution, with a class-action waiver, means you may not be able to go to court to resolve disputes. This can be detrimental if your rights are disregarded or you're part of a larger group affected by DoorDash's actions.

Keep in mind, these Terms of Service are a binding agreement between you and DoorDash, and it's essential to be aware of these provisions before using the service.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DOORDASH CONSUMER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with DoorDash and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised arbitration provisions (including mass-arbitration handling), added DashPass auto-renewal clarifications, updated tipping/refund mechanics and added new sections covering AI-generated menu summaries and order-suggestion features.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by DoorDash to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/DoorDash-Consumer-Terms-of-Service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/DoorDash-Consumer-Terms-of-Service .

**Uber US Terms of Use**

These terms govern your relationship with Uber, which provides services like ride-hailing, food delivery, and more. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Scope:** These terms apply to Uber's products and services, as listed on their official terms page.

**Content and License:** When you use Uber's services, you're sharing content, such as ratings and feedback. Uber might use this information to improve their AI and machine learning systems. They'll follow your settings and relevant laws to use this data.

**Privacy:** For detailed information on how Uber collects and uses your personal data, check their published Privacy Policy. It explains the types of data they collect and how they process it.

**Dispute Resolution:** In case of disputes, binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) is used with a class-action waiver. This means you can't sue Uber in court and file a joint lawsuit with others who had similar issues. However, you have a 30-day window to opt out of arbitration for new accounts.

**Termination:** Either you or Uber can end the agreement under certain conditions, described in the live document.

**Other Provisions:**

- Uber can change these terms at any time.
- If you have questions or concerns, you can check Uber's published legal contact information.

**Potential Concerns:**

- The use of binding arbitration with a class-action waiver might make it difficult or expensive for users to resolve disputes with Uber.
- The fact that the terms can be changed at any time without notice might leave users vulnerable to sudden changes in service or policies.

Keep in mind that this is a summary, and the full text contains more detailed information. It's essential to read the terms carefully and reach out to Uber's support team or visit their support page for more information.

**Please note:** Since this is the first version upload, there's no prior version to compare with. The change log only lists new changes.

**If you have questions or concerns, I recommend reviewing the full text and reaching out to the official support channels instead.**

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — UBER US TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Uber and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised arbitration after the New Jersey Uber Eats arbitration decision, added language on AI-generated trip summaries and driver/rider safety features, and expanded liability sections regarding third-party services.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Uber to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.uber.com/legal/en/document/?country=united-states&lang=en&name=general-terms-of-use . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.uber.com/legal/en/document/?country=united-states&lang=en&name=general-terms-of-use .
